name: Flags
description: Shows the race flags on an 8×8 LED matrix (Arduino, ESP32 or ESP32-C3 running the PitFlag firmware), with animations you can edit.

settings.label: Device port
settings.description: The USB port the board is plugged into.

settings.label: Animation pack
settings.description: The set of animations the matrix plays.

settings.label: Show green for
settings.description: How long the green flag stays up after the start or a restart.

settings.label: Animate outside a race
settings.description: Plays a slow animation when no session is running.

settings.label: Matrix
settings.description: Both are 8×8. WS2812B needs one data pin; MAX7219 needs three.

settings.label: Data pin (DIN)
settings.description: Leave empty to use the board's default pin.

settings.label: Clock pin (CLK)
settings.description: MAX7219 only. Leave empty to use the board's default pin.

settings.label: Chip-select pin (CS)
settings.description: MAX7219 only. Leave empty to use the board's default pin.

settings.label: Color order
settings.description: Most panels are GRB. If red shows as green, try RGB.

settings.label: Correct LED colors
settings.description: Lowers green and blue a little, so yellow does not look lime.

settings.label: Zigzag wiring
settings.description: On when each row runs the other way from the one before. Most 8×8 panels do.

settings.label: Rotate
settings.description: Clockwise, as you look at the matrix.

settings.label: Current limit
settings.description: Keep it at or below what the USB port or power supply gives. A USB port gives 500 mA.

settings.label: Board
settings.description: The microcontroller, not the matrix. PitFlag is built for it.
